body.statement: Assume \(d_e(G)<\infty\), a valid source-prime chart package \(\mathfrak C_{G,e}\) is supplied, and fix a successful finite output of \(\mathrm{thm:conditional\mbox{-}geometric\mbox{-}resolution}\). On \(\mathcal K_G\), every nonzero denominator, specialized-leading-coefficient, and squarefreeness factor in \(h_{G,e}\) has a positive minimum in absolute value by continuity and compactness. Hence every rational-circuit coefficient of the finite monic polynomial \(p_e\) is uniformly bounded, and the monic Cauchy bound confines all \(d_e(G)\) complex roots to one fixed disk. The root-incidence set over \(\mathcal K_G\) is compact; because the squarefreeness factor does not vanish, \(\partial_t p_e\) has a positive minimum in absolute value on that set. Consequently there is \(\gamma>0\) such that every two distinct complex roots, and therefore every two distinct retained real roots, are separated by at least \(\gamma\), uniformly over \(\mathcal K_G\).
body.proof_tex:
Put \(d=d_e(G)\).  On the successful finite-output event,
\[
 p_e(\Sigma,t)=t^d+\sum_{a=0}^{d-1}c_a(\Sigma)t^a.
\tag{21}
\]
Each \(c_a\) is a rational covariance circuit.  By \(\mathrm{def:regular\mbox{-}class}\), \(\mathcal K_G\) is compact and lies in \(\mathcal M_G\setminus\mathcal E_{G,e}\).  Thus every denominator, specialized-leading-coefficient factor, and squarefreeness factor occurring in \(h_{G,e}\) is continuous and nonzero on \(\mathcal K_G\).  Each has a positive minimum in absolute value, while every numerator has a finite maximum.  Hence there exists \(M<\infty\) such that
\[
 \max_{0\leq a<d}|c_a(\Sigma)|\leq M
 \qquad(\Sigma\in\mathcal K_G).
\tag{22}
\]
If \(z\) is a root and \(|z|>1+M\), then
\[
 |z|^d
 \leq M\sum_{a=0}^{d-1}|z|^a
 =M\frac{|z|^d-1}{|z|-1}
 <|z|^d,
\tag{23}
\]
a contradiction.  Hence all roots lie in the fixed disk \(|z|\leq1+M\).  The incidence set
\[
 \mathcal Z_{\mathrm{root}}
 =\{(\Sigma,z)\in\mathcal K_G\times\mathbb C:p_e(\Sigma,z)=0\}
\tag{24}
\]
is closed in a compact set and is therefore compact.

The nonzero squarefreeness circuit says that \(p_e(\Sigma,\cdot)\) and \(\partial_t p_e(\Sigma,\cdot)\) have no common root.  Thus \(\partial_t p_e\ne0\) on (24), and continuity gives
\[
 \eta=\min_{(\Sigma,z)\in\mathcal Z_{\mathrm{root}}}
 |\partial_t p_e(\Sigma,z)|>0.
\tag{25}
\]
Suppose that no uniform root separation existed.  There would then be \(\Sigma_\nu\in\mathcal K_G\) and distinct roots \(z_\nu,w_\nu\) with \(|z_\nu-w_\nu|\to0\).  Compactness provides a subsequence for which \(\Sigma_\nu\to\Sigma_*\) and \(z_\nu,w_\nu\to z_*\).  The divided difference
\[
 \frac{p_e(\Sigma,z)-p_e(\Sigma,w)}{z-w}
\tag{26}
\]
extends polynomially to \(z=w\), where it equals \(\partial_t p_e(\Sigma,z)\).  It vanishes along the sequence, so passage to the limit gives both \(p_e(\Sigma_*,z_*)=0\) and \(\partial_t p_e(\Sigma_*,z_*)=0\), contradicting (25).  Therefore some \(\gamma>0\) separates every two distinct complex roots uniformly on \(\mathcal K_G\).  By \(\mathrm{def:regular\mbox{-}class}\), the selected class lies in a regular-cell refinement whose retained values are labeled among the real roots of \(p_e\); hence the same \(\gamma\) separates all distinct retained roots.
body.justification: Denominator, derivative, and branch-separation margins follow from the certified exceptional locus and compactness, so none is imposed as a free condition.
body.gap: Standard simple-root perturbation results often posit isolated roots; this lemma records the compact polynomial argument that produces the isolation margin for the certified SEM eliminant.
body.consumer: The finite-set matching and simultaneous branch neighborhoods use derived regularity constants without narrowing the statistical class by an oracle margin assumption.
